newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-GRAF AND CHANG PLAY NURSE IN FIRST-ROUND WINS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF AND CHANG PLAY NURSE IN FIRST-ROUND WINS.

text.p: Steffi Graf and Michael Chang both had to do a spot of amateur nursing on Monday as they cruised into the second round of the Australian Open.
Graf was leading 5-1 against Janette Husarova of Slovakia when her first round opponent collapsed on centre court with a knee injury 22 minutes into their match.

Husarova was forced to wait several minutes before receiving treatment and top seed Graf, who won the match by default, was forced to step in and take a handful of ice cubes to ease her opponent's pain.
"It did take a while for someone to come out," said Graf after the match. "Another physiotherapist would be helpful at the start of a big tournament like this."
Men's world number two Michael Chang also did some first aid during his 6-0 6-3 6-1 routing of Belgian qualifier Kris Goossens.
Chang, who reached the final in Melbourne last year without dropping a set only to lose to Boris Becker, was on top form as he dispatched Goossens in one hour and 35 minutes on an outside show court.
But the second seed had to take a break during the third set when he handed a ball girl a cold towel after she fainted in temperatures hovering around 35 degrees Celsius (95 degrees Fahrenheit).
Chang, who is seeking to win his first grand slam since capturing the French Open as a 17-year-old in 1989, was pleased with his game in the first grand slam of the year.

"It is always good to get off to a good start in the early rounds when the top players can falter a bit here in the first tournament of the year and get some nerves out of the system," he told reporters.
Graf said she was surprised by the amount of injuries in Melbourne and the number of players forced to withdraw before the Open even started.
To the dismay of tournament organisers, some of the game's biggest names are absent, most notably 1996 women's champion Monica Seles, who is nursing a broken finger.

World men's number four Yevgeny Kafelnikov withdrew last week after breaking his hand and local star Mark Philippoussis, who ousted world number one Pete Sampras from the tournament last year, pulled out on Sunday because of tendinitis.

In other action on Monday, 15th seed Michael Stich saw off Sweden's Patrik Fredriksson 6-3 6-2 6-2 and women's third seed Conchita Martinez of Spain enjoyed a 6-0 6-2 win over Miriam Oremans of the Netherlands.
The youngest woman in the draw, 15-year-old Russian Anna Kournikova, made an early exit, losing 6-2 6-2 to 12th seed Amanda Coetzer of South Africa.
Kournikova, who reached the fourth round of last year's U.S. Open, had been seen as an outsider to watch.
One player celebrating was Tamarine Tanasugarn, who achieved what she said was Thailand's best grand slam result with a 6-3 1-6 6-4 victory over Elena Makarova of Russia.
